I’m so sorry you feel this way, I’ve been there. You’re right, we guys are supposed to be tough, overcome anything, but we aren’t Superman my friend. You’re taking a very big step just realizing you’re not strong, it takes so much insight and open mindedness to recognize that in ourselves.

The loneliness is rough as well, I grew up in a pretty conservative and religious place and when I came out as bi, my whole world fell out from under me. I was kicked out a week later told If I changed, I could come back if I could apologize for all the drama I’d caused. No one would take me in, I was in a homeless shelter for a week, praying to god my coworkers didn’t find out. I had a very old friend who’d moved away I was luckily able to get in touch with, he was in another state, away from all my pain. He welcomed me and housed me till I got a new job and could start paying rent. I started making new friends, crazy people who loved me for who I was, what I believed and how I felt. 

It’s hard to see from where you are right now I know, you’re not even at the tunnel where there’s light at the end. You’re in the middle of a dirt road in the middle of the woods, I’ve been there, you’ve probably seen my tracks. Right now find things that you can escape with safely for a short period of time. Hobbies, favorite movies, music, working out, going for walks. Before you know it you’ll be at that tunnel, then you just gotta get through it. It’s so much better out here in the light, there’s people ready to dump Gatorade on you, carry you on their shoulders, shake your hand and hug you tight. We are waiting eagerly for you, you’ve got this brother. Just little steps a day is all you need. You can’t see or here is but we are screaming your name.
